feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-heavy roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and dense, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Good impact evidence: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and tool stack details make achievements believable.  
- Strong positioning: the summary and skills sections consistently support a digital strategy/communications leadership brand.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Soft Skills” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than business impact; include clearer outcomes where possible (engagement growth, efficiency gains, revenue/member impact, adoption improvements).  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “more than 12 years experience” should be “more than 12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs later lists without final comma); “organization-wide” and dash usage are mostly good but should be standardized throughout. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience. Tightening the language and foregrounding recent leadership in digital transformation will make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with your current market value: digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven communications leadership.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a tighter grouping such as “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel communications, web modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, editorial workflow design, and digital systems that improve coordination, governance, and audience engagement. Strong background in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap heavily with Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” is already reinforced in multiple NACo roles, so keep it brief here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of strategic, technical, and operational strengths, but several items are broad and overlap heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value, distinctive capabilities will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, senior-level terms: “Multi-channel communications leadership,” “CMS modernization & web operations,” “Editorial systems & governance.”
- Reduce repetition by combining similar items: merge “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture” into one systems/governance competency.
- Align style for parallel structure and consistency; use either all nouns or all noun phrases.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial systems, workflow & governance • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Data analytics & reporting” and several platform-related items overlap with Topline Skills/Technical + IT.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project footer. Tighten around 3–4 high-impact outcomes and name the organization if possible.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership association, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one outcome-focused line: “Improved cross-channel communications operations by redesigning digital workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make Drupal/CMS work more concise and specific: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits; provided front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public sites.”
- Add measurable outcomes wherever available: launch dates, traffic, number of publishers/teams supported, reduction in publishing time, search relevance gains, or campaign engagement metrics.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this bullet brief unless you remove the footer project.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats NACo and Core Competencies language; emphasize what is new in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and distinguish this director-level role from your earlier NACo positions. Emphasize transformation, team leadership, and infrastructure over channel management details already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia operations, and budget oversight across web, email, social, and video.”
- Rewrite bullets to stress outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more concrete where possible: add budget size, team size, reporting cadence improvements, production cost savings, or faster publishing/reporting timelines.
- Combine lower-value channel language into one concise bullet and keep the strongest differentiators: Drupal migration, analytics stack expansion, in-house studio build, governance systems.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this at a more strategic level.
- Video/programming language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed as building enterprise in-house production capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what you owned at this level: executional leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function, not “helping”: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show ownership and outcome: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving consistency and delivery speed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in the Director of Digital Media role.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent roles. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize leadership scope and strategic value rather than broad, generic phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing “leadership,” “messaging,” and “planning” styles inconsistently.
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “publishing strategy” if you want stronger alignment with recent work leading systems and workflows.
- If space allows, prioritize terms tied to current senior roles: governance, enterprise web, cross-channel operations, advocacy.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already reinforced in the header and multiple NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too tool-list-heavy and overlaps with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current strengths and platform modernization impact rather than repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a concise capability line: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop older/lower-priority items here unless central to target roles: consider removing jQuery, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages from this topline section.
- Prioritize what recent roles prove best: Drupal, CMS modernization, integrations, automation, and AI-enabled search.
- If space allows, make one phrase outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization and technical execution” instead of just “CMS modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and reserve full platform/tool inventory for the technical section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and the header summary; mention it once here only if it remains a priority differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a generic tool list. It would be stronger if framed around decision-making and business impact, especially since the recent NACo role already proves hands-on use of these platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder from outcome to tools: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis, GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Decision-support reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- Consider “Analytics infrastructure & optimization” as the heading to better match the seniority shown in recent roles.
- If space allows, add one impact-oriented phrase: “dashboarding and insight generation” or “measurement frameworks and reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating every tool here if the Technical + IT section already carries the full stack.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add context on level of use or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Put **Drupal first** and add brief qualifiers only for the most relevant/recent platform; that aligns with your recent experience and strongest differentiator.
- Standardize naming: use **Microsoft Power Pages** instead of “Power Pages” for clarity and ATS matching.
- If space allows elsewhere, move lower-priority items like **GitHub Pages** behind more business-relevant platforms or remove if not used meaningfully in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the **Topline Skills: Web Platforms & Technical Execution** section almost exactly.
- Consider merging this with the Topline Skills entry or using one section for platforms and the other for implementation depth.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support your recent Drupal, AI search, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add light proficiency/context instead of just tools: **Front-end implementation for Drupal sites • API-based integrations • Tag management and deployment automation**
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use versioning; **HTML, CSS, JavaScript** is cleaner.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution** (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations”). Keep the broader summary there and make this section more tool-specific.
- “Workflow automation” is already covered elsewhere; avoid re-adding it here unless tied to **GitHub Actions** or **Cloudflare Workers**.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools** to better match the content.
- Separate true automation tools from project/collaboration platforms for clarity: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show application, e.g. **workflow design, task orchestration, cross-team coordination**.
- Consider dropping one weaker/older PM tool if not current, and keep the list focused on tools most relevant to recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if collaboration systems are genuinely part of your technical positioning.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and platform-focused without repeating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one capability cue instead of more tools: **campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Best final version: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Campaign automation • Audience segmentation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters” or audience scale here; that impact is already covered in the NACo experience bullets.
- Don’t repeat broad “multi-channel communications” language already captured in Core Competencies and recent roles.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can add them.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add 1–2 measurable outcomes if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, weekly video cadence, audience growth, or team/process improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence to emphasize execution: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”
- If space allows, split into 2 bullets for readability rather than one long paragraph.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; here, position it as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating governance/operations language already used more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a notable “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the innovation/program support angle and keep the digital piece tightly framed.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and the standout outcome: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives that supported NACo program development and policy communications.”
- Tighten the multimedia clause and make the podcast the proof point: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If you can, add 1 measurable detail: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders served, or audience/download growth.
- Consider a sharper full version: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy communications; produced digital content and launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid broad “digital content production” language that repeats later NACo roles focused on web, video, and channel operations.
- Don’t overstate multimedia leadership here; later roles already show larger-scale digital/media ownership.
